chapters.title: Artificial Satellites: Humanity's Eye in the Sky
chapters.title_zh: 人造卫星：人类的天空之眼
chapters.body: An artificial satellite is a human-made object intentionally placed into orbit around Earth or another celestial body. Since the dawn of the Space Age in the mid-20th century, satellites have transformed global communications, environmental monitoring, space exploration, and everyday modern navigation. 1. Physics in Orbit: The First Cosmic Velocity To place an object into a stable orbit around Earth, it must achieve a specific horizontal speed known as the First Cosmic Velocity (also called orbital velocity). Gravitational Pull vs. Centripetal Force Satellite Orbit Earth The Physics Formula: By balancing the gravitational pull of Earth with the required centripetal force for circular motion: r GM m r m v v R GM km/s km/h Three Cosmic Velocities: First Cosmic Velocity (v km/s Minimum speed required to achieve low Earth orbit (LEO). Second Cosmic Velocity (v km/s Escape velocity needed to break free from Earth's gravitational pull to reach other planets. Third Cosmic Velocity (v km/s Speed required to escape the Sun's gravitational field and leave the Solar System entirely. 2. Historic Milestones: Dawn of the Space Age Key Milestones in Early Satellite History Sputnik 1 (October 4, 1957): The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 into low Earth orbit. A metal sphere equipped with radio transmitters, its simple "beep-beep" signal marked the official start of the Space Age and triggered the US-Soviet Space Race. Dongfanghong-1 (April 24, 1970): China launched its first artificial satellite, Dongfanghong-1 (东方红一号), aboard a Long March-1 rocket. This milestone made China the fifth nation capable of launching satellites independently. The satellite broadcast the melody of The East Is Red back to Earth via radio. 3. Orbit Types: Geostationary Satellites and Space Stations Satellites operate across various orbital altitudes depending on their operational mission: Orbital Altitudes Around Earth Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) Located along Earth's equatorial plane at an exact altitude of km, a geostationary satellite completes one full orbit in hours, minutes, and seconds—matching Earth's exact rotational period. To observers on the ground, the satellite appears permanently fixed at the same spot in the sky, making GEO ideal for TV broadcasting and regional weather monitoring. Space Stations Are Satellites Too Crewed orbital laboratories—such as the International Space Station (ISS) and China’s Tiangong Space Station (天宫空间站) —are technically massive artificial satellites operating in Low Earth Orbit (km ). They function as long-term research platforms for microgravity science, human medicine, and space engineering. 4. Modern Applications: How Satellites Serve Earth Artificial satellites have integrated into every facet of modern infrastructure: Application Primary Orbit Core Function & Real-World Examples Reconnaissance & Defense Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Optical and radar imaging for military intelligence, missile detection, and border security. Remote Sensing Sun-Synchronous LEO Geological surveying, forestry tracking, agricultural crop monitoring, and disaster damage assessments (e.g., Landsat, Sentinel). Meteorology (Weather) GEO / LEO Tracking hurricanes, cloud formations, atmospheric moisture, and global climate trends (e.g., Fengyun, GOES). Navigation & Positioning Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) Global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) providing real-time location data (e.g., GPS, Beidou, Galileo, GLONASS). Telecommunications & TV GEO / LEO Direct-to-home satellite television, maritime/aviation communications, and internet services. 5. The Commercial Era: Reusable Rockets and Mega-Constellations The commercial space revolution has drastically cut launch expenses over the last decade, transitioning spaceflight from state-monopolized programs to high-frequency private operations. Commercial Spaceflight Transformation Reusable Rocket Economics: Rocket landing techniques (pioneered by SpaceX's Falcon 9) reduced payload launch costs from around kg to under kg, opening low Earth orbit to commercial enterprises. Starlink & Mega-Constellations: Leveraging low-cost launches, companies have deployed thousands of small, mass-produced LEO satellites working in tandem as a internet network (a mega-constellation ), delivering high-speed broadband internet to remote regions, ocean vessels, and emergency disaster zones. 6. The Growing Challenge: Space Debris (Kessler Syndrome) With thousands of active satellites and defunct stages orbiting Earth, space debris (space junk) has become an urgent global safety concern. The Kessler Syndrome Risk High-Velocity Impacts: Objects in LEO travel at km/s. At this speed, even a paint fleck or tiny screw possesses enough kinetic energy to breach spacecraft hulls or destroy active satellites. Kessler Syndrome: Proposed by NASA scientist Donald Kessler, this scenario warns that a high density of objects in LEO could trigger a chain reaction of collisions, where each impact creates fresh debris—eventually rendering specific orbital planes entirely unusable for generations. 7. Beyond Earth Orbit: Planetary Explorers and Mars Satellites Humanity's use of artificial satellites is not confined to Earth. Satellites placed into orbit around other planets act as communication relays and scientific pioneers. Interplanetary Pioneer Relay (Collects Data) (Data Relay Hub) (Scientists Receive) Martian Orbiters: Space agencies have successfully inserted dozens of artificial satellites around Mars—such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), ESA’s Mars Express, and China’s Tianwen-1 (天问一号) orbiter. Pioneering Exploration: These orbiters map planetary topography, analyze atmospheric conditions, locate subsurface water ice, and serve as vital deep-space communication relays between ground rovers (like Curiosity Perseverance, and Zhurong ) and scientists back on Earth.

chapters.body: Modern life has become increasingly inseparable from household appliances. These machines perform heavy labor, regulate indoor climates, simplify cooking, and deliver high-definition entertainment, transforming homes into comfortable and efficient living spaces. 1. Climate and Comfort: Creating an Ideal Living Environment Environmental control appliances regulate temperature, airflow, and illumination, providing a comfortable sanctuary regardless of external weather conditions. Climate Control & Lighting Electric Lighting (电灯): Evolved from incandescent bulbs to energy-efficient LED fixtures, providing steady illumination and customizable color temperatures. Electric Fans (风扇): Provide rapid air circulation and convective cooling at low power consumption. Air Conditioners (空调): Regulate both temperature and humidity, providing precise cooling during heatwaves and efficient heat pump heating in winter. Heating Systems (暖气/暖风机): Maintain ambient warmth during cold seasons via radiators, convection heaters, or underfloor heating circuits. 2. Kitchen Appliances: Crafting Culinary Variety at Home Kitchen appliances streamline food preparation, thermal cooking, preservation, and cleanup, allowing households to cook diverse, restaurant-quality meals efficiently. Food Storage & Thermal Cooking Refrigerator (冰箱): Preserves fresh produce and halts bacterial growth through low-temperature refrigeration and freezing compartments. Microwave Oven (微波炉): Uses electromagnetic radiation to excite water molecules in food, reheating meals in seconds. Electric Oven (电烤箱): Uses radiant heating elements to bake, roast, and brown pastries and meats with precise temperature control. Air Fryer (空气炸锅): Circulates superheated air via rapid convection to produce crispy textures with minimal cooking oil. Toaster (吐司炉): Uses localized heating coils to crisp sliced bread quickly for morning meals. Food Prep & Sanitation Blender (搅拌机): Purees soups, emulsifies sauces, and blends smoothies using high-speed rotating steel blades. Electric Whisk / Mixer (打蛋器): Aerates liquid ingredients, whips egg whites, and emulsifies batters for baking. Dishwasher (洗碗机): Uses high-pressure hot water jets and specialized detergents to wash and dry crockery automatically, saving water and labor. Disinfection Cabinet (消毒柜): Employs high heat, ozone, or ultraviolet light to sanitize tableware and eliminate surface pathogens. 3. Hygiene & Cleaning: Maintaining Personal and Home Sanitation Hygiene and cleaning appliances automate repetitive physical chores, ensuring personal grooming and maintaining domestic cleanliness. Hygiene & Cleaning Operations Washing Machine (洗衣机): Automates soaking, agitating, rinsing, and spin-drying fabrics, drastically reducing manual domestic labor. Water Heater (热水器): Supplies continuous hot water via gas combustion or electric heating elements for showers and domestic sanitation. Hair Dryer (吹风机): Directs focused warm airflow to evaporate moisture from hair safely and rapidly. Vacuum Cleaner (吸尘器): Uses suction motors and cyclonic filtration to lift dust, dander, and debris from carpets and hard floors. Robotic Vacuum (扫地机器人): The autonomous evolution of the vacuum cleaner, combining suction, self-navigation (LiDAR/cameras), and obstacle avoidance to clean floors without human intervention. 4. Home Entertainment: Immersive Leisure and Recreation Entertainment appliances provide digital media, gaming, and relaxing leisure experiences within the home. Television Sets (电视机): Evolved from cathode-ray tubes to ultra-thin 4K/8K OLED and QLED displays, acting as central hubs for news, sports, and cinematic streaming. Gaming Consoles (游戏机): Dedicated high-performance computers that render real-time 3D graphics for interactive home entertainment. 5. Evolutionary Trend: From Manual Knobs to Smart Automation The evolution of appliance controls reflects broader shifts in human-computer interaction, progressing toward hands-free automation. Evolution of Control Interfaces Manual Switches: Early appliances required physical interaction—flipping switches, turning mechanical dials, or setting manual timers. Infrared Remote Controls: Introduced wireless convenience, allowing users to adjust televisions, air conditioners, and audio systems from a couch or bed. Smart Home Integration: Modern appliances connect to home networks via Wi-Fi or Zigbee. Users can monitor energy usage, schedule washing cycles via smartphone apps, or control appliances hands-free using voice assistants. 6. Household Electrical Safety Guidelines While appliances offer unprecedented convenience, improper usage carries risks of electrical shock, short circuits, or electrical fires. Key Safety Rules Keep Water and Electricity Separated: Never operate switches, plugs, or electrical appliances with wet hands, particularly in humid areas like bathrooms and kitchens. Avoid Outlet Overloading: Do not daisy-chain multiple high-wattage appliances (e.g., air fryers, space heaters, microwave ovens) into a single power strip. Inspect Wiring Regularly: Check power cords for frayed insulation or exposed copper wires. Replace damaged cables immediately. Unplug When Idle: Unplug heating appliances (toasters, irons) when not in use to prevent accidental thermal ignition.

chapters.title: The Six Major Nutrients
chapters.body:
Your body needs six important nutrients to work well. They are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.

Carbohydrates give your body energy. You can find them in rice, noodles, bread, and potatoes. If you do not get enough, you may feel tired and weak.

Proteins help your body grow and repair itself. They are in meat, fish, eggs, beans, and milk. Without enough protein, children may grow slowly, and muscles may become weak.

Fats also give energy and help keep your body warm. They protect your organs. Nuts, seeds, fish, and cooking oil have fats. But too much fat is not good.

Vitamins help your body use food and fight sickness. Fruits and vegetables are full of vitamins. If you lack vitamins, you may have problems with your eyes, skin, or gums.

Minerals, such as calcium and iron, are very important. Calcium makes bones and teeth strong. Iron helps your blood carry oxygen. Milk, green vegetables, and meat give you these minerals. If you lack them, your bones may be weak, or you may feel very tired.

Water is also a nutrient. It carries things around your body, controls your temperature, and removes waste. If you do not drink enough water, you may feel thirsty, dizzy, or sick.

To get all six nutrients, eat many different foods every day. Choose rice, vegetables, fruit, eggs, milk, beans, and fish. Drink enough water. Eat less candy and junk food. A balanced diet helps you grow, learn, and stay healthy.

chapters.title: Proteins: The Amazing Machines of Life
chapters.body:
Proteins are important molecules in every living thing. They are made of smaller units called amino acids. There are about twenty common amino acids. Cells join them in different orders to build many kinds of proteins. This order is decided by our genes.

Proteins do many jobs. Some help chemical reactions happen. These are enzymes. Some build muscles, skin, and hair. Some carry oxygen in the blood. Others fight germs and keep us healthy.

People need protein in food to grow and stay well. Our bodies can make some amino acids, but not all. The ones we cannot make are called essential amino acids. We must get them from foods like eggs, milk, beans, fish, and meat. Eating different foods helps us get all of them.

A protein is not just a long chain. It folds into a special shape. The shape helps it do its job. If the shape changes, the protein may stop working.

Scientists have long wanted to know how proteins fold. In recent years, an AI program called AlphaFold has predicted the shapes of many proteins. This helps doctors and scientists understand life and design new medicines.
